Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The players walk out to the middle. Suzie Bates and Sophie Devine are the openers of New Zealand Women. Jahanara Alam to start with the ball.
... The Chase ...

Right then! The hosts need 141 off 162 deliveries to open their accounts. Not a big target but New Zealand need to approach the target in a positive way. Bangladeshi spinners will play a key role here and they need to be tight with their lengths. Second half coming your way shortly....

Frances Mackay is up for a quick chat. She says that after the disappointment of the last match they needed a strong performance here. She adds that she is happy to contribute to the cause and they did really well to pull back things. Also mentions that the curators have done a fantastic job and the surface looks good to bat on, reckons the girls will do the job with the bat.

Bangladesh will be slightly disappointed. They started really well and deserved to finish things in a positive way but wickets tumbled and that made their work cut out. The opening pair of Shamima Sultana and Fargana Hoque put 59 runs. Sultana fell but Hoque did well to stay in the middle and keep the scoreboard ticking. She brought her fifty but some lazy footwork saw her giving away a wicket. Other than that, no one contributed much and they finish on 140. Bangladesh will feel they are 10-15 runs short here. Are they? Time will tell though...

A good toss to win you reckon. At first, Sophie Devine would have questioned her decision but once the Powerplay was over, The White Ferns grew in the game and started to build the pressure. Once they got the wicket of Sultana, the gates opened and wickets started coming regularly. Amy Satterthwaite got two wickets in her first over while others contributed with good bowling. Frances Mackay got one wicket and also contributed with two run outs. Overall, a good performance from New Zealand Women.

Finally, we got a game after that rain show very early on. It is wet and the outfield is very slow but the ground staff has done a really good job to make the ground ready. Talking about the contest, a superb comeback from New Zealand Women and they will be very happy with the way things worked out after that early carnage by Bangladesh Women.
Tossed up, around off. Lata Mondal steps out and drives it down to wide long off for a single. Bangladesh Women end with 140/8!
Nahida Akter comes in.

OUT! RUN OUT! Make that three run-outs now! On off, this is nicely swatted away towards deep mid-wicket by Jahanara Alam. The batters hesitate a bit in going for the second and Alam has to scamper back. Amelia Kerr in the deep throws it towards the bowler. Amy Satterthwaite does really well to reach forward and collect the ball. She then wastes no time in knocking over the bails. The dive doesn't save Alam and she is a goner.
On off, heaved down to long on for a single by Lata Mondal who has lost her bat as well. They look for the second but it isn't available.
Satterthwaite sees Mondal stepping out and fires it in full. Mondal cannot get the ball past the bowler.
A bit fuller, on off. Alam sweeps it along the ground towards deep square leg for one more.
A tad shorter and wider, cutaway to point for a quick run.

Three again! This is pushed wider, Lata Mondal skips down the track and looks to big downtown. She gets a thick outside edge which runs away towards the third man region. The ball clogs a bit and the batters come back for the third.

New Zealand Women have taken the review for LBW. Looks very close. No bat there and the angle makes the ball goes away from the wickets. Not out is the answer. This was full and angling around middle and leg. Alam gets low to sweep but misses and gets hit on the pads. An appeal for LBW but not given. They take it upstairs but the wickets were missing. A leg bye taken in the process.
On middle, driven through mid on for one.

OUT! RUN OUT! Another run out and it's Frances Mackay again who shows brilliant ability in the field. Looped up, around off. Salma Khatun steps out and pushes it towards extra cover. Khatun goes for the quick run but Suzie Bates does well to spring to her right and collect the ball. She releases it quickly but the underarm throw is a bit wide. Mackay though does well to pouch the ball and stretch a bit to whip off the bails. On the replay, one can see that Khatun is well short.
Is that run out? The batter is already walking back. Ohh, she is miles away from her crease. Again impressive work from Frances Mackay.
Brilliant running once again! On middle, flicked through square leg and they pick up another couple of runs. Valuable runs these for Bangladesh Women.
Tossed up, outside off. Salma Khatun dances down the track and pushes it back to the bowler.
Outside off, Mondal edges it down to short third man.
Very full, around off. This is played towards cover.
Drizzle has started again. The umpires will look to finish the innings in the meantime.

Excellent running! On off, Salma Khatun goes for the reverse sweep now and gets it really fine. The fielder from short third man gives chase and slips a bit due to the wet outfield. The batters seize the opportunity and race back for the third.
Two more! This is slowed up, on a length and outside off. Khatun looks to cut again but the ball comes off the gloves and goes past the keeper.
A bit short and wide, Salma Khatun cuts it behind point and races back for the second.
On the pads, turned through mid-wicket for a single.
Brilliant bowling! Another dot! Tossed up, on middle. Khatun can't get it past mid on.
On off, driven straight back to the bowler.
Fullish delivery, outside off and skidding on. Khatun gets beaten on the outside edge as she looks to cover drive.
A touch flatter and wider, cutaway towards cover-point.
On middle, pushed through mid on for a single.
Lata Mondal walks in.

OUT! RUN OUT! Frances Mackay with a brilliant piece of fielding! This is looped up, full and on off. Fargana Hoque steps out and pushes it to the right of the bowler. Mackay pounces on the ball and takes advantage of the lazy work from Hoque. Mackay shatters the stumps with a direct hit and the keeper reckons it's out. The replays roll in and show that Hoque did not have her bat grounded in time. Fargana Hoque has to depart after a fighting knock and New Zealand Women in control of the game here.
Is that out? Quick work from Frances Mackay and Fargana Hoque is in trouble. The replay shows her bat was in the air when the ball hits the bails. Superb work.
Fuller ball, around off. Hoque tries to lay on the leg side but gets a leading edge to covers for a single.
Salma Khatun is the new batter in for Bangladesh Women.

OUT! CAUGHT! Amy Satterthwaite gets her third wicket and 50th overall in ODI! A fuller ball, outside off. Moni charges down but toe ends her shot, in the air and to mid off where Sophie Devine tracks back and takes it. New Zealand chipping away with wickets regularly.
Commentary.Howout: c Sophie Devine b Amy Satterthwaite

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! On the charge rightaway! Tossed up, on middle. Moni slogs-sweeps it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
On middle, eased to long on for one.

Short again, much slower this time but Hoque dabs it gently to third man for a couple of runs. Fifty for Fargana Hoque! She needs to give the finishing touch now. Gets applause from her teammates as well.
SHorter ball, outside off. Fargana cuts it past point for a brace.
A fuller ball, outside off. Hoque dabs it to short third man for a single.
Ritu Moni is in at number 6.
OUT! TAKEN!  A timely wicket for New Zealand! This is full and outside off, was the slower ball.  Mostary slogs it but without much power. Maddy Green at deep square leg takes it with ease.
Commentary.Howout: c Maddy Green b Hayley Jensen

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller ball, on middle. Hoque shuffles across and tucks it to square leg for a single.
Short and outside off, pulled in the gap, to deep mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Flatter and on middle. Hoque blocks it out
Short, straying on middle, Mostary pulls it to long on for a single. A slip at the non-striker's end denies another run.
Hayley Jensen (2-0-13-0) is back on.
Around off, fuller and Mostary hits it to square leg for a single.
FOUR! Much needed and that brings up the 100 for Bangladesh! Flighted ball, outside off. Mostary skips down, drives it hard and through covers for a boundary.
On middle, tucked to mid-wicket for one.
Slightly short and on middle, this is worked to deep square leg for one.
Now a short ball, on middle, Hoque pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Floated, full and outside off, pushed to covers.
On middle, eased down to long on for another single.

Did Katey Martin spill that catch? It looks like it. Fullish delivery, around off. Mostary leans in and looks to work it leg side but gets a faint bottom edge. Martin has almost no time to get her gloves low and pouch the catch. The ball goes off her pads and towards short fine leg. They get a single.
Pitched up, around off. Hoque drives it down to long off for one more.
Another slower ball, on middle. This is worked through mid-wicket for a run.
Slower one, bowled into the pitch and pushed wider. Sobhana Mostary looks to pull but cannot get it past mid on.
A length ball, outside off. Hoque works it through covers for one.
Very full and wide, slapped to sweeper cover for just another single. The boundaries have completed dried up at the moment.

Well bowled! This is flighted and drifted into middle. Fargana Hoque looks to flick it leg side but gets beaten in flight. The ball goes off the leading edge and past the keeper towards third man. They get two.
A bit of width on offer and this is tapped through the cover region for a single by Mostary.
On middle, clipped away towards mid-wicket.
Tossed up, outside off. Hoque heaves it down to long on and picks up a single.
Very full, around off and this is drilled straight towards silly mid on.
Full and wide, driven towards cover. A maiden over for Jess Kerr to start her comeback spell!
Very full, on off. Defended out.
Length again, well outside off. Mostary is unable to pirce the cover region and the dot balls are mounting up.
Pitched up, on off. Mostary drives it down towards mid off.
A length ball, outside off and this is tapped towards point.
Jess Kerr gets away with one there! Short and wide, slapped away but straight to the fielder at point.
Tossed up, full and outside off. Sobhana Mostary strokes it through covers and looks for two. They decide against it in the end.
Floated up, Hoque drives it through the cover region for a single.
On  middle, flicked away to mid-wicket.
Tossed up on middle. Hoque looks to straight drive but the ball just holds up in the surface. The checked drive is easily stopped by the bowler.
Around middle, this is paddled away towards fine leg. The batters look for two but have to settle for one.
A yorker on off. Mostary squeezes it out on the leg side.
A lot of flight on this one. Hoque defends it off the front foot.
Very full and on middle. Hoque jams it out towards mid on.
Looped up, on off. Mostary pushes it down to long on for a single.
Tossed up, on off. Mostary drives it nicely but can't get it past the fielder at extra cover.
On middle, worked through mid-wicket.
A bit of extra bounce now! Flighted, on a length and outside off. The ball holds its line and beats the outside edge of Hoque's blade.
Sobhana Mostary is the new batter for Bangladesh.

OUT! BOWLED! Starts the over with a wicket and ends with one as well. Good start by Amy Satterthwaite! Tossed up, fuller and outside off which spins back in as well. Rumana Ahmed gets on her knees as he tries it sweep but gets an inside edge onto the stumps. Good comeback from New Zealand after that busy Bangladeshi period.
Very full, eased down to long on for a single.
Short, slower and outside off, Ahmed  punches it through point for a single.
Full ball, outside off. Ahmed steps across and pushes it to point.
Slower, on a length, on off. Ahmed waits and blocks it out.
Rumana Ahmed walks out to bat at number 4.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! First ball of Amy Satterthwaite's spell and she gets a wicket! Shorter ball, outside off, it was well wide and Nigar Sultana went for it with a big cut but gets an outside edge to Katey Martin, behind who gobbles it up. New Zealand finding the groove at the right time.
Commentary.Howout: c Katey Martin b Amy Satterthwaite

Commentary.Commentary: Amy Satterthwaite to have a bowl now.
A single as this is swept to deep square leg for a single.
On middle. Sultana comes down the track and smashes it straight down the ground. The fielder from long on comes across and dives a bit early but safes a couple in the end.
Tossed up, outside off, pushed to mid off.
FOUR! Finally a shot of aggression! Fuller and on off. Sultana slogs it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Slightly short, on middle, pulled to deep square leg for a single.
Tossed up, on middle, tucked to mid-wicket.
Just a single then! A googly, on off. Sultana on the back foot, chops it on the off side.
Fuller again, on off. Sultana knocks it to covers.
A floated ball, on off, pushed to mid off.
On the pads, flicked to short fine leg for a single.
Fuller and skidding through, on off. Hoque defends this one.
Tossed up, on the pads. Kept out.

Drinks! Well, given the overcast conditions one would have expected the White Ferns to have got a lot more purchase early on but Sultana and Hoque came out all guns blazing and treated the opposition attack to some feisty shots. The pair have given their side the platform to get to a big total but Frances Mackay has got the hosts back into the game with that wicket. It is nicely poised here at the moment.
A full toss, on off. Hoque sweeps it to deep square leg for a single to end the over.
On middle. Defended.
Fuller and outside off, Hoque drives it through covers and a couple of runs are taken.
A flighted full toss, outside off, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Very full and this is drilled down to long on for a single.
Tossed up, fuller and outside off. Hoque tries to defend inside the line and misses it.
Very full and on middle. Hoque hits it to mid on and a misfield allows a single. New Zealand have done really well to slow things down.
Fuller ball, outside off. Sultana prods to defend and gets an inside edge to square leg for a single.
A googly, outside off, cut away to point for a single.
Tossed up, on middle. Hoque prods and blocks it.
On middle, pushed nicely but straight to mid on.
Fuller and on middle, Nigar sweeps it to square leg for a single.
Full and straight, eased down towards long on for a run.
Very full, on off and dipping on the batter. Sultana blocks it out.
Length this time, angling into middle and leg. Hoque works it on the leg side for a single.
Beaten! Drifted in from around off but the ball just holds its line. Hoque strides out to defend but gets beaten past the outside edge.
Nigar Sultana walks out to the crease.

OUT! TAKEN! Pace off the ball has done the trick for New Zealand Women! Frances Mackay comes into the attack and breaks the opening stand. This is delivered on a length, around off. Shamima Sultana fetches it and tries to swipe across the line. Sultana ends up getting a top edge which flies towards backward square leg. Lea Tahuhu races in from the fence and slides in to take a very good catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Lea Tahuhu b Frances Mackay

Commentary.Commentary: On off, this is stroked away towards mid off.
Full, on off. This is swept away behind square for another single.
On off, Shamima Sultana tries to be cheeky and looks to scoop it over the keeper's head. She misses and gets hit around the helmet.
On a length, around middle and turning back in sharply. Sultana defends it out off the back foot.
Short and wide, cutaway off the back foot by Hoque towards deep point for one more.
On off, nicely swept away to deep square leg for a run.
This is floated up on off. Sultana drives it straight towards mid on.
Full again, on off. This is pushed towards cover.
A low full toss, angling into middle and leg. Fargana Hoque flicks it well in front of square on the leg side and picks up an easy brace.
This is pushed wider, Sultana looks to cut but gets a bottom edge down to third man for one.
Shorter this time, around off. This is pulled away through mid-wicket for a run.
Full and straight, pushed towards mid on.
A length ball, on middle. Hoque hangs back and jabs it over the mid-wicket region for a couple of runs.
Tossed up again, outside off. Hoque drives it along the ground towards deep cover for a single. The fifty comes up for Bangladesh Women. They are off to a flier here.
Nicely tossed up, around off. This is pushed towards cover-point.
On off, swept away behind square on the leg side for one.

Bye! Beaten all ends up! A lovely flighted delivery, on off. This one dips on the batter who is pushed forward. The ball turns back in and deceives the batter as well as the keeper. They do get a bye.
Good running! Around off and a bit fuller. Sultana nudges it towards point and sets off for a quick single.
Flatter delivery, angled into leg stump. Hoque rocks back and squeezes it out to short fine leg for a single.
Amelia Kerr is into the attack now.
A big swing and a miss! Pitched up, around off and again the ball swings it very late. Sultana hangs back and looks to swing it away leg side but misses.
Full and wide, stroked towards point.
FOUR! Anything short is being punished here! Shorter in length, on middle. Shamima Sultana pulls it uppishly and into the square leg fence for another boundary.
Fullish again and on off. Sultana blocks it out.
Kerr goes fuller, on off and there is late in-swing on offer. Sultana pushes it towards mid on.
On a good length, swinging back in from well outside off. Sultana dabs it down towards gully.
Powerplay done! The fielding side can now have up to 5 fielders outside the 25-yard circle.
Fuller and around off. Hoque blocks it to covers. Super start for Bangladesh, they are off to a flier.
Through the gap! Fuller and outside off. Sultana punches it through cover-point for three runs as deep backward point cuts it out.
On off. Kept out.

In the air but safe! Short in length, outside off. Sultana hooks it past mid on. The ball does not have legs to race away and it stops near the ropes. Sultana thought it is a boundary but she has to run now.  Two taken in the end.
Slightly short, outside off. Sultana hits it aerially to point.
A length ball, outside off. Sultana slaps it through diving point for two runs.
Hayley Jensen comes into the attack and she will bowl the final over of the Powerplay.
Short in length, on middle, pulled to deep square leg for one more.
Slants a full ball, on middle, pushed to mid on.
On a length, on middle, swinging in and Sultana nudges it to mid-wicket.
On a length, outside off, cut to third man for a single.
This one comes with the angle, on middle. Sultana glances it square on the leg side for one.
A length ball, big boomer inswing and Sultana keeps it out.
Angles it on the pads, flicked to deep square leg for one.
FOUR! Intent from Bangladesh! Short of a length, on off. Sultana pulls it to mid-wicket again for a boundary. Tahuhu is livid with herself.
Fuller ball, outside off. Shamima drives and misses.
Wide! Bangs a bouncer around off. Sultana watches it sail over and collects a wide.
FOUR! On a length, outside off. Sultana gets low and sweeps it over mid-wicket for a boundary. Really good from Sultana.
On middle, tucked to mid-wicket for a single.
A length ball, outside off. Hoque smashes it through mid off and Sophie Devine gives a chase to save a couple of runs. Good start by Bangladesh.
Around off. Blocked out.
Short in length, on off. Hoque looks to pull but gets a top edge to fine leg and the ball drops safely before the fielder comes across. One.
A length ball, inward movement, on the pads, Hoque tickles it to the fine leg region for a couple.
Wide! New Zealand have not yet settled! A fuller ball, swings late past the right-hander as she tries to flick but misses.
Again comes back in nicely, short and on middle, pulled away to deep square leg for a brace.
This one jags back in sharply, on middle. Sultana plays with the angle to square leg and takes a quick single. Hoque makes the other end with a good dive.
FOUR! Touch fuller and outside off. Sultana slaps it through cover-point for a boundary.
A full ball, outside off and it nips back in. Sultana offers no shot. Wide.
Jess Kerr to operate from the other end.
FOUR! Hoque is underway! Short of a length, around off. She pulls it to mid-wicket for a boundary.
Full, straight and on middle, flicked to mid-wicket.
A length ball, outside off. Hoque leans and guides it to the gully region.
Short of a length, on middle. Sultana pulls it to deep square leg for a single.
A length ball, angling around middle and leg. Sultana looks to flick but gets an inside edge onto the pads. An appeal for LBW  but there was some bat present.
On a length, on off. Defended out.
Wide! Tahuhu starts with a length ball, way outside off. Sultana sees the delivery and leaves it alone.

We are ready for play! The umpires and players are out in the middle and are raring to go. There's a slight drizzle out there but New Zealand Women are all set to play. Finally, the opening pair of Shamima Sultana and Fargana Hoque make their way out to the middle. Both sides take the knee to show their support for the BLM movement. Lea Tahuhu has the new ball in hand and is ready to steam in. Let's go...

We are moments away from the start of play and it is the first-ever meeting in an ODI game between these two sides. First, the teams will line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Bangladesh's national anthem first followed by the national anthem of New Zealand. Also, the game is now reduced to 27 overs per side instead of the 28 as stated earlier. Two bowlers can bowl 6 overs and 3 can bowl 5. The Powerplay will be 5 overs and there are no floodlights at the venue so it might get a little gloomy later on.

PITCH REPORT - Simon Doull is pitchside. He says the ground staff did a brilliant job. Tells it will skid on, there is dampness and DLS might come into play later on and bowlers should enjoy the condition.

Nigar Sultana, the Bangladesh Women captain says they would have liked to bowl first given the weather conditions. Informs that they have made a couple of changes to the side. She adds that the bowlers have shown great character and they have had good preparation for this match. She also mentions that whether a full game or a reduced game, they want to play their brand of cricket.

New Zealand Women skipper, Sophie Devine says they will bowl first. Adds, the preparations are going on and they have two changes as well. Tells, after the loss they had some conversation and they are ready to take on Bangladesh now. Mentions, Bangladesh played really well against South Africa and they are looking forward to this clash.

Bangladesh Women (Playing XI) - Shamima Sultana, Nigar Sultana (C/WK), Rumana Ahmed, Fargana Hoque, Ritu Moni, Sobhana Mostary (In for Sharmin Akhter), Salma Khatun, Lata Mondal (In for Murshida Khatun), Jahanara Alam, Nahida Akter and Fariha Trisna.

New Zealand Women (Playing XI) - Sophie Devine (C), Suzie Bates, Amelia Kerr, Amy Satterthwaite, Maddy Green, Frances Mackay (In for Brooke Halliday), Katey Martin (WK), Hayley Jensen (In for Fran Jonas), Lea Tahuhu, Jess Kerr and Hannah Rowe.
TOSS - New Zealand Women have won the flip of the coin and they have elected to BOWL first.

UPDATE 7.05 am IST (1.35 am GMT) - It's the news every cricket fan has been waiting for. The rain has stopped for quite a while now and the news from the ground is that a 28-over game will take place starting at 7.35 am IST (2.05 am GMT). The covers are off and only the pitch is under covers at the moment. The overhead conditions are still pretty grey but hopefully we do not get another rain intervention and the game can finally get underway.

UPDATE 6.05 am IST (12.35 am GMT) - Unfortunately there hasn't been any significant change in the weather conditions and it is still raining. Another inspection has been set for 6.30 am IST (1 am GMT). Also the cut-off time for a 20-over game is 8.38 am IST (3.08 GMT). So, the conditions will have to improve really quick for the groundsmen to have any chance of clearing all the water and take care of any dangerous patches formed. Let's hope for the best for now.

Update 5 am IST (11:30 pm GMT, previous day) - No changes in the weather as it continues to rain. We have started losing overs as well. An inspection will take place at 5:30 am IST (12 am GMT). Stay tuned for further updates...

Update 4 am IST (10:30 pm GMT, previous day) -The conditions have gone better but still, it is drizzling. The ground staff and the officials are out in the middle as the covers are still on. They have to wait for the rain to stop and after that, an inspection will take place. Let's hope for some positive news. Stay tuned...

Update 3:01 am IST (9:31 pm GMT, previous day) - First and foremost, there was rain overnight and it is raining currently as well. So, the toss is delayed due to rain. The good thing is the drainage is very good here at Dunedin but for now we wait for the conditions to get better. Stay tuned with us for further updates...Next update is scheduled at 4 am IST (10:30 pm GMT, previous day).

Bangladesh are a side that is getting better and better every year and now they are going head-to-head with the biggest teams in Women's cricket. They bowled really well in their first game against South Africa and seemed well on course of providing a major upset as they got off to a pretty good start with the bat as well. Their inexperience at the big events though got the better of them in the end. Bangladesh will however will be ready for the big challenge that they have in front of them and cannot be taken lightly. So, will we see the hosts suffer another shock loss? Or will they sweep Bangladesh aside? We'll find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit.

The hosts came into the World Cup back on the form a thumping series win against India and an impressive showing in the warm-up matches as well. However, the White Ferns seemed to be feeling the pressure of the host nation as they failed to get over the line against the Windies in their opening encounter. The skipper though found her form with the bat yet again and they will be looking to put on a statement performance today against Bangladesh.

The Women's World Cup has got off to a flying start and each team has now played one match each. During the weekend we saw a couple of rivalries reignited and we saw a couple of absolutely thrilling finishes as well. Today, the hosts New Zealand Women take on Bangladesh Women in match number 5. Both sides lost their opening encounter and will be looking to get teir first points on the board. On that note, a very warm welcome to the coverage.
... MATCH DAY ...
